newsitem.title: GREECE: SUSPENDED WORK TO RESUME QUICKLY ON ATHENS METRO.
newsitem.headline: SUSPENDED WORK TO RESUME QUICKLY ON ATHENS METRO.

text.p: Halted construction work on parts of Athens new metro will resume "within the next few days" and there is no question of negotiating a new contract, Greek Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis told reporters.
He was speaking after talks with representatives of the Attiko Metro management and the construction consortium Olympic Metro.
Olympic Metro, a consortium of 23 Greek and foreign firms -- including Germany's Hochtief and Siemens -- has halted work on four of 50 sites and stopped two large tunnel digging machines.
"We agreed that work would start again at the four stations and the process to start the tunneling machines would begin. We will meet again in 15 days," Laliotis said.
A senior source at Attiko Metro told Reuters that a dispute over money would be discussed at the next meeting.
Laliotis added: "Any effort for a new contract will mean a new bidding process and a new contractor. I told them that no Greek government would accept a new contract."

The source said that Olympic Metro was now talking about the need for an additional 60 to 70 billion drachmas to complete the metro. Attiko Metro officials have said they would pay a maximum of 20 to 25 billion drachmas more. --Costas Paris, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
